A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOOZY study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original eight-task evaluations, training-stage and case-aggregator ablations, pathologist assessments, and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports additional held-out evaluations and a new training-stage ablation.

M1.justification: The two-stage architecture and objectives remain. Section 3 changes the case transformer from using DropPath to explicitly disabling it, also specified in v3 Table 16. This is a limited reported regularization revision. The slide-encoder LayerScale correction does not establish another architecture change: v1 Table 11 already specified it as disabled.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from eight to sixteen tasks. Added coverage includes TCGA-BRCA, HNSC, and UCEC molecular subtyping; HANCOCK keratinizing/non-keratinizing SCC grading and primary-versus-metastatic classification; and VALENTINO RAS/BRAF status and synaptophysin grading. The original tasks and stated 56-dataset training coverage remain.

E2.justification: The external slide-encoder, patch-encoder, and MIL comparator sets remain unchanged. Within the ablation comparison, v3 adds Stage 2 only without the case aggregator as a directly evaluated comparison configuration in Table 3 and new Table 31.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Table 17 revise Stage 2 training from 12 epochs, 600 steps, and approximately 307 GPU-hours to 20 epochs, 1,000 steps, and approximately 512 GPU-hours. The new from-scratch mean-pooling control also extends the evaluation design. Five-fold probing, metrics, and probe optimization remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a targeted ablation removing both SSL initialization and the case transformer, with task-wise results in new Appendix M/Table 31. Existing stage and aggregation ablations extend to sixteen tasks. The attention-map, embedding-visualization, PCA, and neighborhood-stability analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-fold means and standard deviations and retain the same bootstrap neighborhood-stability procedure. Additional result rows use existing reporting practices; no new seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear across MLP, linear-probe, MIL, and ablation tables. The original eight-task numerical entries are retained exactly. MOOZY's macro F1/AUC/balanced accuracy changes from 0.801/0.815/0.758 to 0.769/0.763/0.702 over the expanded task set, not a same-setting performance decline. New results expose molecular-subtyping weaknesses, and TITAN leads sixteen-task macro AUC at 0.768 versus 0.763.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations for self-distillation, survival losses, spatial sampling, prediction heads, attribution, and embedding geometry remain unchanged after matching appendix moves. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central patient-first, two-stage contribution remains. Headline performance claims shift from best-or-tied performance across the original tasks to leading macro F1 and balanced accuracy across sixteen tasks. The introduction also broadens novelty from the first open and reproducible framework to the first method jointly addressing slide representation and explicit inter-slide modeling.

C2.justification: v3 replaces strong assertions that aggregation gains confirm unique inter-slide information with more qualified reporting of gains and regressions. It discusses the aggregator's poorer performance without SSL and explicitly excludes dense or segmentation predictions. The acknowledged lack of evaluation requiring deeper multi-slide reasoning remains.

D1.justification: v3 explains singleton supervised cases when case identifiers are unavailable, replaces 30,024 unique patients with 41,089 supervised cases, and revises Table 6 accordingly. It clarifies that the existing aggregation ablation discards the transformer only at inference and specifies disabled DropPath. Some preprocessing and patch-pretraining details are removed; the code link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the HANCOCK and VALENTINO dataset papers and cites the already-listed MIL-Lab work in the supervised-encoder discussion. Positioning shifts somewhat from open reproducibility toward inexpensive supervision, while the novelty claim loses its open-and-reproducible qualification. The broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, results discussion, and conclusion are condensed or revised, with more consistent case-aware terminology. A new appendix subsection shifts subsequent lettering. The overall section sequence and most methodological and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a three-panel display with separate sixteen-task MLP and linear-probe radars. Main and appendix result tables expand substantially, Table 3 gains a configuration, and a new Table 31 is inserted. Training-data tables move closer to their discussion, and multiple figures are relocated; most underlying qualitative visuals are retained.

improvement.justification: The broader evaluation exposes performance limits absent from v1's eight-task results, while the additional control and clearer case and ablation definitions improve empirical transparency. Claims and applicability boundaries become more informative. These gains are limited by the still-unresolved evidence for deeper multi-slide reasoning and the less-qualified novelty claim; they do not establish an improved model under matched settings.
